title: From Hourly Rates to the Max Verstappen Salary: Converting Your Pay to Annual, Fortnightly, and Tax
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes the max verstappen salary comparison, tax estimates, and superannuation.
salarySummary: Using a 38-hour week and 52-week year, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour equates to $52,270.40 annually before tax.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This is your gross annual pay before tax and other deductions.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). Superannuation is calculated on the total ordinary earnings including casual loading.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% on $45,001 to $135,000, 37% on $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. A 2% Medicare levy generally applies. Use the Australian Taxation Office's gross pay estimator for an estimate.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: The 38-Hour Week, the Fortnight, and the Max Verstappen Salary

Whether you're negotiating a new job offer or just curious how your hourly rate stacks up, converting to an annual salary is straightforward. The standard formula used across Australia is **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For most full-time employees, the hours per week is 38, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog). This article walks you through the conversion, explains the fortnightly equivalent, and shows how tax and super fit in. And yes, we'll even touch on the **max verstappen salary**—a reported figure in the millions—to show how the same formula scales up.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52.

If you work 38 hours a week, the calculation is:

**Annual = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026, per the Fair Work Ombudsman), the annual amount is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,270.40

That's your gross pay before tax, Medicare, and any salary packaging. The same formula works for any hourly rate, from a junior award rate to the **max verstappen salary** (reportedly around $55 million per year from his Red Bull contract). If Max were paid by the hour at that annual figure, his hourly rate would be roughly $27,800—but of course, elite athletes have very different pay structures.

### Why 38 Hours?

The 38-hour week is the standard full-time benchmark under most modern awards and the National Employment Standards. It's the figure used in the Fair Work Ombudsman's [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) calculations. If you work part-time or casual, your actual hours may differ, but the conversion method stays the same.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply double your weekly pay:

**Fortnightly = hourly rate × 38 × 2**

Using the minimum wage: $26.44 × 38 × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight. This is useful for budgeting and comparing with pay slips.

### Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most industries have specific awards with higher minimum rates. For example, the Children's Services Award and Pharmacy Award recently received increases due to the Fair Work Commission's gender-based undervaluation review. Always check the relevant award using the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides to ensure you're being paid correctly.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not getting paid leave. The casual minimum wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, tick the casual loading checkbox to add the 25% automatically. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading—the tool adds it for you.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It does not come out of your hourly rate. For 2026–27, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. So if your annual salary exceeds that, super is capped. For the minimum wage example, super would be $52,270.40 × 12% = $6,272.45 per year, added to your retirement savings.

### Tax Estimates

Once you have your annual gross pay, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (based on 2025–26 reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a minimum wage earner, tax would be roughly $5,092 plus Medicare, leaving about $45,000 take-home. Use the Australian Taxation Office's gross pay estimator for a personalised estimate.

### Putting It All Together: A Real Example

Let's say you earn $35 per hour as a full-time permanent employee.

- Annual gross: $35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160
- Fortnightly gross: $35 × 38 × 2 = $2,660
- Super (12%): $8,299.20 paid on top
- Estimated tax (2026–27): about $11,467 + Medicare $1,383 = $12,850 total deductions
- Estimated take-home: $56,310 per year

If you were casual at $35 + 25% loading = $43.75 per hour, your annual gross would be $86,450, with super on top.

### The Max Verstappen Salary Comparison

To put it in perspective, the **max verstappen salary** is reported to be around $55 million per year. Using the same formula backwards: $55,000,000 ÷ 52 ÷ 38 ≈ $27,800 per hour. That's over 1,000 times the minimum wage. While most of us won't reach those heights, the conversion method remains the same—hourly rate times hours per week times 52.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more accurate calculations, use the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) and the ATO's online tools. And remember, whether you're on the minimum wage or chasing the **max verstappen salary**, the maths is the same.
